transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Solutions), Alex (NimbleHealth SRE), Samira (Platform), Jordan (Head of AI), Tariq (Security)

Summary:
Quick workshop to walk through a recent production degradation NimbleHealth hit (sporadic 95th/99th token latency spikes), show console traces, explain fallthrough/fallback routing, and propose a trial Dedicated run to validate mitigations. Discussed security needs and next steps for a pilot.

Topics: request tracing, KV cache vs prefix caching, fallback model routing, request playback, error forensics, security & SOC2, trial Dedicated capacity

Action items (captured verbally above).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: all right good afternoon everyone thanks for taking the time. quick roll call - maya from redwood, ethan se, priya solutions. can you hear me on the customer side?
[00:12] Alex: yep loud and clear alex here, samira, jordan and tariq as well.
[00:18] Ethan: great, we got the incident notes you shared, thanks for that — saw the spike graph around 11/30 and the request example IDs. we want to walk the trace together and show how the console surfaces the KV cache miss pattern and the fallback to the larger model.
[00:33] Jordan: yes that's the one — about 2% of requests suddenly ballooned to 800-1200ms p99 for token generation, normally we're sub-200ms.
[00:44] Priya: thanks for the context. just to set expectations, we'll use the live console demo telemetry, but sanitized — we'll also show a playback so you can see the decoded request and how kv cache keys diverge. some of the transcription in the exported traces can be noisy, so call that out.
[00:59] Samira: quick Q up front: are we going to see how routing rules might send traffic to a cheaper variant? we worry about quality when things fall through.
[01:12] Ethan: yep, exactly. show two routes: primary low-latency quantized model and fallback to high-accuracy full model. when the KV cache misses and sequence length grows, the runtime may trigger fallthrough; that raises token compute and latency.
[01:28] Alex: in our infra we saw a pattern where prefix caching wasn't as effective because different prompt prefixes changed a lot — so we get less reuse. could that be a cause?
[01:40] Ethan: absolutely. prefix churn reduces effective cache hit rate. console traces show prefix similarity score (approx) and you can filter by cache-hit vs miss. note some of the metric labels might be transcribed as K V cash in the export, so ignore the artefact.
[01:58] Jordan: (laughs) yeah we thought it said K V cash the first time too.
[02:05] Maya: okay let's share screen — bringing up the incident trace now. you should see request waterfall, token timeline, and the model routing pane.
[02:18] [screen share noise]
[02:25] Ethan: here's the waterfall — the green spans are runtime prep, blue are model decode. notice at ~t+120ms there's a cache lookup and then a miss, after miss we see a fallback to the larger model. p95 shot up shortly after.
[02:42] Samira: is there a way to replay the exact request with the same tokenization locally? we'd like to reproduce.
[02:50] Priya: yes, request playback exports the prompt + token stream. you can run it in a sandbox or request-level replay in the console — we include environment tags and seed so the behavior matches. caution: some providers obfuscate tokenization differences.
[03:07] Alex: we also saw intermittent 5xx from an internal proxy right when the spikes happened. could that be causing retries and amplifying latency?
[03:15] Ethan: absolutely possible. console timeline shows adjacent network errors and retry loops — the trace highlights retry count and which component (proxy vs runtime) returned the error. often retry amplification is the dominant factor, not just model time.
[03:32] Jordan: that matches our suspicion — the spike windows line up with proxy pool resizes we did.
[03:37] Maya: good note, so mitigation options: 1) adjust retry/backoff at proxy, 2) change routing to restrict fallthrough during low-capacity windows, 3) increase Dedicated reserve for the 2-week test to see if it eliminates capacity-based routing to slower variants.
[03:54] Samira: curious on (2) — how hard is it to set routing policy per route? we have multiple services using the same model endpoint with different SLOs.
[04:04] Ethan: it's per-route config — you can set latency SLO thresholds, preferred model variants, and auto-fallback rules. console UI shows active policy and you can simulate policy impacts with traffic replays.
[04:15] Tariq: on security, we need to confirm data residency and key management — do you support customer-managed KMS and can logs be stored in our VPC?
[04:25] Priya: yes, Private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC-hosted logs. hosted API can also integrate with your KMS for encryption at rest, plus we have an audit log export for your SIEM. we'll attach the SOC2 excerpt and the private-deploy checklist after the call.
[04:42] Alex: perfect. also, for the playback we want anonymized exports — is that automatic?
[04:48] Maya: playback can be configured to redact PII fields at export time. we'll include the redaction config in the docs.
[04:55] Jordan: can we get a concrete test plan? like ramp 5% traffic to Dedicated reserve and run a 48h soak?
[05:02] Ethan: yes we can provision a small Dedicated pool, route a percent of traffic for controlled weeks. we'll work with your infra to verify QoS.
[05:12] Samira: about costs — our finance will ask how the Dedicated billing looks when we're in a trial. we don't want surprise usage charges.
[05:19] Maya: trial Dedicated is usually arranged as a capped commit for test window; we'll send explicit pricing with caps and the expected per-token delta in the sheet.
[05:28] Alex: can you show the console view for an end-to-end request now — token timing, model selection flags, and any attached logs?
[05:35] Ethan: jumping back to the trace, here's the per-token timeline — you can hover to see kernel selection and whether quantized kernels were used. the console labels may show 'q8' or 'fp16' but sometimes the auto-labeling miscalls exact quantization level in the transcript export.
[05:51] Jordan: interesting, so if we detect a sequence growth pattern we could proactively pin to high-capacity nodes?
[05:57] Ethan: we have a routing rule that pins sessions whose prefix similarity falls below threshold to the higher throughput pool — that reduces fallthrough during long sessions. it's a balance: cost vs predictability.
[06:09] Priya: showing request logs panel — search by request ID, trace ID, or user token. you can also jump to full span JSON. note: sometimes the auto-transcribed speaker labels are off in exports, so timestamps are more reliable than speaker tags.
[06:30] Samira: we noticed some logs had scrambled hostnames in the export, maybe due to our masking rules. can we get raw logs on demand?
[06:37] Maya: yes with Private or Dedicated we can provide raw log export to your S3/VPC bucket; in hosted we provide scrubbed exports with an option for more detail under NDA.
[06:49] Alex: any defensive instrumentation we should add to our side to pin down root cause faster?
[06:54] Ethan: two quick ones — incrementally sample KV cache keys and add a correlation id on ingress so the trace spans persist across your proxy and our runtime. that makes end-to-end attribution much easier.
[07:06] Jordan: we can add correlation ids, should be straightforward.
[07:10] [noise / typing]
[07:20] Maya: switching to playback demo — I'll trigger a replay of ID 9f8a2. you should see the same token timing and the cache lookup.
[07:29] [short silence]
[07:35] Ethan: see the replay timeline? there's a microburst at token 42 where backend queued a couple requests. you can download the full replay bundle from the console.
[07:50] Samira: okay we'll pull that and run locally. any gotchas on determinism?
[07:55] Ethan: hardware differences and TPU vs GPU tokenizers can change outcomes slightly. we recommend using the same container image for replay.
[08:05] Tariq: on compliance: does Redwood keep full request logs longer than 30 days by default? we need 90-day retention for audits.
[08:13] Priya: default retention is 30 days, enterprise plans allow configurable retention up to your requirement and longer exports for audit periods. we'll include retention options in the checklist.
[08:25] Alex: can the console alert on rising cache-miss rates automatically?
[08:30] Ethan: yes, create a metric rule for cache_hit_ratio and set thresholds; console will fire alerts and can trigger a route change or traffic pause.
[08:40] Jordan: good — we want to automate a temporary pause of fallthrough in critical windows.
[08:46] Maya: that's doable — the route policy supports automated fallback disable for a time window when an alert fires. we'll demo the rule config in the follow-up session.
[08:56] Samira: can we script route changes via API as well? we prefer IaC.
[09:01] Priya: yes full API support and Terraform provider for routes, model variants, and alerting. we'll send the provider examples.
[09:12] Alex: anything on cost/quality tradeoff for sticking with quantized vs full precision during spikes?
[09:18] Ethan: quantized models give big token cost reductions but degrade some output on edge cases. routing policies can be made content-aware so critical prompts route to full models. it's a pragmatic hybrid.
[09:30] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[09:34] Maya: recap: Maya will share pricing and trial onboarding doc; Ethan will export the demo trace bundle + a sample script to replay; Priya will send SOC2 excerpt and Private deploy checklist; NimbleHealth (Samira/Alex) will share the slow request ids and decide on trial scope. schedule follow-up week of 2026-12-20 for runbook + policy simulation.
[09:54] Samira: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[09:57] Jordan: thanks, appreciate the walkthrough.
[10:00] Maya: end of recording. we'll follow up via email with the attachments.
